classes.roman-run-in-letter-slot: French reading and listening number a question's sub-parts (i), (ii), (iii). The census files them in its letter slot, and the generic continuity check expects a letter run a, b, … there, so every complete roman run reports a letter-gap. The flagged run is complete from (i), every part in it is covered by a card, and reconciliation has no orphan, so no card cites a part the census lacks. Not a missing part.
classes.joint-tariff-pair: The scheme prices two printed questions together (a shared tariff), so the census keys the pair under the first number and the second number is absent from the run. The paired leaf text prints both questions ("Question n: … Question n+1: …"); the reading ledger reviewed these shared boundaries. Not a missing question.
classes.stem-of-priced-parts: The flagged block is question-shaped but is the stem (or the Irish rendering) of an ask whose priced parts are separate census leaves, each covered by a card. Checked on the rendered paper page.
classes.reviewed-scoring-decision: The scheme heading prices the ask at one value while it prints a per-answer value for a two-answer ask and the comprehension total only reconciles at the per-answer value. The reading ledger holds a reviewed scoringDecision for exactly this fault (same text), with paper and scheme page evidence, and the card is priced and disclosed accordingly.
classes.printed-total-differs: The 2021 and 2022 written booklets print their own smaller totals on the cover (Higher 130 marks, Ordinary 140 marks; listening 80 / 100), so the sitting sums to 210 / 240 rather than the 300 / 320 of other years. Both booklets are present and read, and every printed ask is covered. Not a lost booklet.
